Build Task Ledger, an offline personal task application, as BOTH an installable Android APK and a native Windows EXE. Start from an empty project using the supported Android Kotlin/Compose and Windows C++ scaffolds. I want working applications with the same behavior on both platforms, not a web mockup, an explanation, a counter demo or a single empty screen. Use the app name Task Ledger. Do not add paid services, accounts, advertising, telemetry, network requests or external dependencies. Keep the scaffold's Gradle settings and dependency versions unchanged so the installed offline toolchain can build it.

I use fairly long descriptions and I need you to retain the details near the end of this request just as carefully as the beginning. Read the full saved requirements before implementing. You can split the source into small files. A successful compiler run by itself is not enough: implement the behaviors below, write useful tests, inspect their results, repair genuine failures, and review every requirement against the final source before delivery. Do not declare missing features complete because a scaffold exists. Preserve the original application ID and signing identity through any repairs or follow-up changes. The two applications share a data format, not a live connection: there is no server or cloud synchronization in this request.

The main screen has a Title input, a multiline Notes input, a Priority input accepting 0, 1 or 2, an Add button, a Search input, a filter with All, Active and Done choices, a selectable list of tasks, and buttons Save edit, Toggle done and Delete. Selecting a row loads its current values into the editing inputs. Saving an edit updates that same task rather than making another task. Add makes a new task regardless of selection. Show counts of all tasks, active tasks and completed tasks separately from the currently filtered rows. Display a clear inline error after invalid input; leave the saved list unchanged. Controls must stay usable when the Android keyboard is open and on a narrower Windows window. Text typed into the prompt fields must remain visible against the background. Long row titles should wrap or scroll rather than covering the action buttons.

Each task has a positive integer ID, title, notes, priority and completion flag. IDs are immutable and monotonically allocated. Deleting a task must not cause its ID to be reused. New tasks start active. Priority 0 is low, 1 normal and 2 high. The Title input is trimmed only at its ASCII whitespace boundaries before validation; internal whitespace and Unicode characters must be preserved. Reject a title that is empty after that trim or exceeds 240 UTF-8 bytes. Reject notes over 4096 UTF-8 bytes and priorities outside 0..2. A rejected add or edit must not partially change task data or the next available ID. Notes may contain tabs and newlines. Do not strip or reinterpret those characters. Unknown IDs must never edit a different row: edit and toggle should fail, while removing an unknown ID should return false.

Search matches a substring in the title OR notes, using ASCII case-insensitive matching. Non-ASCII text is preserved and can match exactly; do not claim locale-aware case folding. An empty query matches every task. All includes every task, Active includes only unfinished tasks and Done includes only completed tasks. Apply search and completion filtering together. Preserve insertion order when filtering, editing or toggling completion. Derived counts refer to the entire ledger, never just the visible search result. Toggling a completed task makes it active again. Deleting the selected task clears selection. Do not accidentally remove all tasks when only one row was selected.

Data must survive closing and reopening the application. Save successful mutations to a private application file. Android should use its private files directory; Windows should use a TaskLedger subdirectory of LOCALAPPDATA, not the installation directory or current working directory. Write a temporary file and then replace the previous file so a failed write does not destroy the last good data. An invalid or unsupported saved file must produce an explicit error and must not be silently treated as an empty ledger and overwritten. Do not delete an existing valid file as a shortcut to make startup succeed. Keep persistence separate from the UI so it can be tested without a phone or desktop window.

Use this versioned UTF-8 interchange representation exactly. The first line is DSGPT_TASK_LEDGER, a tab, version 1, a tab, the next unused positive ID, then a newline. Each subsequent nonempty row is ID, completion as 0 or 1, priority, Base64 of UTF-8 title, and Base64 of UTF-8 notes, separated by tabs and ended by a newline. Base64 uses the standard alphabet with padding and no line wrapping. An empty notes value is an empty final field, not a missing field. Reject malformed headers, unsupported versions, invalid IDs, repeated IDs, non-increasing allocation state, invalid completion values, invalid priorities, invalid Base64/UTF-8 or invalid decoded titles/notes. Loading is transactional: parse and validate the complete new state before replacing the old state. A failed load leaves the old rows and next ID unchanged. A successful round trip retains IDs, order, flags, priorities, Unicode and multiline notes.

For repeatable independent behavioral testing, expose a small domain API in addition to the UI. This is an acceptance contract, not a request to fake a self-test result. In Kotlin, place TaskLedger and its data classes in the scaffold's application package, in a file named TaskLedger.kt. Define data class Task(val id:Int, val title:String, val notes:String, val priority:Int, val done:Boolean) and data class LedgerCounts(val total:Int, val active:Int, val completed:Int). TaskLedger must expose add(title:String, notes:String="", priority:Int=1):Task; edit(id:Int,title:String,notes:String,priority:Int):Task; toggle(id:Int):Task; remove(id:Int):Boolean; visible(query:String="",filter:String="all"):List<Task>; counts():LedgerCounts; serialize():String; and load(text:String):Unit. Invalid operations throw IllegalArgumentException. In C++, provide windows/task_ledger.h with the equivalent Task, LedgerCounts and TaskLedger in namespace ledger. Use std::string for text, std::vector<Task> for visible, int for IDs/counts, bool for flags and std::invalid_argument for invalid operations. Keep the domain implementation usable from ordinary C++17 on Linux as well as Windows; put platform window and file APIs in separate code. The application itself must use this domain implementation, not a separate untested implementation.

Use stable accessible labels so the actual interfaces can be checked. Android editable fields have content descriptions Title, Notes, Priority and Search; buttons are labelled Add, Save edit, Toggle done and Delete; the filter choices are All, Active and Done. Rows display '#<id> <title> | Priority <number> | Active' or the same ending in Done. Counts display 'Total: <number> | Active: <number> | Done: <number>'. On Windows, use window class dsGPTTaskLedgerWindow and native control IDs 101 for Title, 102 for Notes, 103 for Priority, 104 for Search, 105 for the All/Active/Done filter, 106 for the task list, 107 for counts, 108 for errors, and 201/202/203/204 for Add/Save edit/Toggle done/Delete. These labels and IDs allow an external test to exercise the application; do not implement a special acceptance mode that bypasses normal UI behavior.

Examples that must work: adding '  Alpha  ' with notes 'line1' followed by a newline and 'line2', priority 2, produces title Alpha and preserves the notes. After toggling it done, adding the title 雪 with empty notes and priority 0 produces a separate active task. Serializing those two records has header nextId 3, followed by row 1 with done 1, priority 2, title Base64 QWxwaGE= and notes Base64 bGluZTEKbGluZTI=, then row 2 with done 0, priority 0, title Base64 6Zuq and an empty final notes field. Searching LINE2 finds Alpha even though that text appears only in notes. Filtering Active finds 雪. Restoring the serialized form into a new ledger must preserve those facts. Adding a third record after deleting row 2 must allocate ID 3, not ID 2.

Test add, trimming, Unicode retention, multiline notes, validation without mutation, edit identity, toggle in both directions, deletion, combined search/filtering, whole-ledger counts, serialization round trip, the golden representation above, rejected malformed imports preserving existing state, and monotonic IDs after deletion and reload. Add meaningful Android JUnit tests and portable Windows tests.cpp. Build both requested formats with the actual compiler tools and read any failure diagnostics before repairing. Keep test results and final artifacts. State honestly that compilation and portable tests do not substitute for actual Android/Windows UI tests. Do not claim physical phone testing or universal application-building reliability. Finish only after both current APK and EXE exist, tests pass, and all saved requirement sections have been reviewed.
